name: English
intro: Wand Browser lets HTTPS websites use Bluetooth Low Energy and NFC on iPhone. Explore the open source browser, try the hardware fixtures, and build websites that connect to nearby devices and NDEF tags.
requirements: Requires iOS 18 or later and a physical iPhone for hardware access. The app interface is currently English. Websites need HTTPS, a top-level page, and a foreground session. Each site needs your permission; grants end on navigation, reload, backgrounding, or revocation.
install: Get started with the installation instructions on GitHub. Open this site in Wand Browser, then open the hardware fixtures. A public TestFlight invitation is not yet available here.
bleGuide: Tap “Choose Bluetooth device” to open the device picker. This fixture filters for devices whose names start with hito or Hito and requests the Hito service UUID. Select your own compatible test wallet; the fixture connects to its GATT server and reports connection events. Other websites must request their own filters and services. Pairing alone does not grant a website access.
nfcGuide: Tap “Scan NFC” and hold a compatible NDEF tag near the top of your iPhone. The console shows record types and payloads. Stop the scan before switching tasks. To write, use your own writable test tag: enter text and tap “Write NFC text”, or test a binary record. Writing replaces tag content. This fixture does not read payment cards or emulate NFC cards.
trouble: If an action fails, read the console error, check iOS Bluetooth or NFC permissions and the site controls, then retry in the foreground. After navigation or backgrounding, request permission again. The simulator cannot verify radio or tag operations. Test with real hardware; cancel pickers and check that denied access stays denied.
fixtureIntro: These actions use the browser’s hardware APIs. Select only your own test wallet and writable test tags.
readingError: NFC reading ended or failed. Open site controls and look for “Scan again”.
supportDescription: Get help with Wand Browser, Bluetooth, NFC, website permissions and website data on iPhone.
supportContact: Need help, found a bug or have a feature request? Email {email} or {issues}.
supportSafety: Include your iPhone model, iOS and Wand versions, steps to reproduce, and relevant website and device or tag model. Remove private information from screenshots and logs. Never send passwords, recovery phrases, private keys or sensitive tag contents. GitHub issues are public.
supportStart: Requires iOS 18 or later. Bluetooth and NFC require a physical iPhone and compatible hardware. Try {fixture} in Wand or visit {product}.
supportBleTitle: Bluetooth device not appearing or connecting
supportBle: Enable Bluetooth in iPhone Settings and allow Wand access. Keep the device nearby, awake and advertising. Website filters and services must match it; the fixture only lists names starting with hito or Hito. Choose the device in Wand’s native picker; pairing in Settings alone does not grant website access. If connection fails, check for connections elsewhere and retry. Wand supports a subset of Web Bluetooth using BLE GATT services and characteristics.
supportNfcTitle: NFC tag not reading or writing
supportNfc: Start the website’s scan and hold a compatible NDEF tag near the top of your iPhone while the system NFC interface is open. Keep Wand in the foreground; restart scanning if the timed session ends. Writing needs a writable NDEF tag with enough capacity and replaces existing contents: use your own test tags. Web NFC does not read payment cards or emulate NFC cards.
supportPermissions: Hardware APIs require a top-level HTTPS page and Wand in the foreground; embedded frames cannot use the bridge. Approve the website request and choose the Bluetooth device to share. Access ends on navigation to a new document, reload, backgrounding or revocation in Site controls. Request access again afterwards. Check Site controls if access was denied.
supportDataTitle: Clear website data or browsing history
supportData: Use Site controls → Clear website data to remove storage, cookies and caches. This can sign you out and removes saved per-site fullscreen preferences. Use Clear beside Recent pages on the home screen to remove browsing history. These are separate actions.
